killedBy: classifyPad: how a pad is matched requires EVERY present matcher field, so a near-miss is not a match
why: Turns the last two matcher fields from requirements into passes, so a pad with the wrong axis or button count still matches an entry. The failure this guards is a device acquiring a layout measured on a DIFFERENT device: axis and button counts are the cheapest evidence that an adapter is in the mode a profile was written for, and issue #606 leans on exactly those 'robust browser-reported characteristics'. The killing test sweeps four one-field-off pads rather than one, so a matcher that went permissive in any single field is caught rather than only a wholesale OR.
